title: Voronoi screen on a surface
summary: Scatters random points on a surface, builds 3D Voronoi cells around them and uses the cells to cut a perforated, thickened screen - a typical organic facade or pavilion skin.
how_to_use: Right-click 'Srf' and Set one Surface for your own screen (a sample is stored).
'Number of Points' sets how many cells; 'Cell box X/Y/Z' must be large enough to contain the whole surface.
'Rib width' (0..1) insets the cell outlines on the surface for the flat version in step 3.
'Shell thickness' thickens the surface; 'Cutter offset' shrinks the cells before cutting.

'Run cutter script' is saved OFF in this copy (the original was saved on). Switch it to True only when you are ready: the Python script temporarily adds geometry to the Rhino document and runs the _OffsetSrf command, then cleans up. Switch it off again before changing inputs.
If the cut fails, check the Rhino document tolerance (see the original author's notes) - very small tolerances make the Breps fail.
concepts: Populate Geometry: random points on a surface
Voronoi 3D: cells around each point inside a box
Brep | Brep intersection: cell outlines on the surface
Data Dam: holding back heavy downstream work
Solid Difference: cutting the cells out of a thickened surface
A GhPython script that drives a Rhino command (and why it must not run in parallel)

steps.title: 1  INPUTS - change these
steps.explain: Surface, number of cells, the size of the box that holds the Voronoi cells, offsets, and the toggle that runs the cutting script.

steps.title: 2  Voronoi cells around random points
steps.explain: Populate Geometry scatters points on the surface. A Center Box around the surface centroid limits space, and Voronoi 3D grows one cell around each point. Clean Tree removes empty results and a Data Dam holds them until the heavy steps below are needed.

steps.title: 3  Flat version: cell outlines on the surface
steps.explain: Intersecting the surface with the cells (Brep | Brep) gives the cell outlines lying on the surface. Offset on Srf insets them by 'Rib width' - useful for a laser-cut or flat panel version.

steps.title: 4  Thicken the surface into a closed shell
steps.explain: Offset Surface creates the second skin. The bounding-box faces at both ends are scaled up and intersected with the two skins to build end caps, and Brep Join closes everything into one solid shell.

steps.title: 5  Shrink the cells into cutters (script)
steps.explain: Grasshopper's own offset cannot offset these solids, so a GhPython script hands each cell to Rhino's _OffsetSrf command (only while 'Run cutter script' is True). The shrunken cells become the cutters; their outline is previewed on the surface.

steps.title: 6  RESULT - perforated screen
steps.explain: Solid Difference subtracts all cutters from the shell, leaving the perforated screen. Move places the result next to the input so both stay visible. Bake Move to keep it.
